title: Security governance readout: SOC 2 & ISO27001 alignment - Cypress DataWorks
summary: Redwood team walked Cypress DataWorks through SOC 2 and ISO 27001 artifacts available in the Trust Center, discussed controls mapping spreadsheet, and alignment for a pilot private deployment. Key items: provide SOC 2 Type II report, enable trust-center read-only view for compliance team, clarify KMS options (cust-managed vs Redwood-managed/HSM), SSO test plan, and audit log export for 12 month retention. Customers want formal controls mapping and proof of key separation for production PII workloads in the EU.
next_steps: Evan to share latest SOC 2 Type II (redacted) and ISO27001 summary by 2026-08-14
Maya to provision Trust Center read-only link and instructions for evidence download by 2026-08-16
Tom and Maya to schedule SSO test (SAML) and RBAC walkthrough week of 2026-08-24
Evan to collect KMS integration notes and EKM/HSM options and send by 2026-08-18
Rui/Aisha to review controls mapping doc and provide feedback by 2026-08-21
action_items: Evan Cross - Send redacted SOC 2 Type II and ISO summary (due 2026-08-14)
Maya Patel - Create Trust Center read-only invite + download guide (due 2026-08-16)
Maya & Tom - Run SSO/SAML test in staging and confirm RBAC roles (target week 2026-08-24)
Rui Chen - Return first-pass controls mapping comments (due 2026-08-21)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-11 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Evan C., Maya P., Luis G. — Redwood; Aisha K., Tom B., Rui C. — Cypress DataWorks

Summary (auto): Quick readout of security posture, trust-center artifacts available, and mapping for SOC 2/ISO. Action items captured.

[00:00] Evan Cross: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Evan with Redwood Inference, I'm the account exec on this. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Aisha Khan: Hi, Aisha here, head of infosec at Cypress.
[00:07] Tom Becker: Tom, cloud architect.
[00:09] Rui Chen: Rui, compliance.
[00:11] Maya Patel: Maya, solutions engineer, I'll run through the controls and trust center.
[00:14] Luis Gray: Luis from customer success, here to help with onboarding.

[00:30] Evan Cross: Cool, objective for today is to show what artifacts we have for SOC 2/ISO, walk a controls mapping we started, talk KMS choices for key control, and SSO/RBAC steps. We'll aim to leave with clear next actions.

[01:02] Aisha Khan: Sounds good. We're most concerned about key ownership and whether we can keep keys in our Cloud HSM for EU production data. Also audit log retention for 12 months and proof we can map controls to our policy.

[01:25] Maya Patel: Great, we'll cover that. Quick note, some of the names in our docs may show Redwood Dedicated or Redwood private, sometimes the transcript generator miswrites it as "redwood dedicate" so bear with me.

[01:50] Tom Becker: Ha, okay. Also, we have an internal policy that requires SSO via our corporate IdP, SAML, and scoping of granular roles before we store any PII.

[02:12] Evan Cross: Understood. On the SOC2 piece — we have a redacted Type II we can share. Maya, can you walk the trust center access?

[02:25] Maya Patel: Yeah. In Trust Center we've got the SOC 2 Type II PDF, an ISO27001 scope summary, and a controls evidence catalog. I can provision a read-only link to the trust center for Cypress compliance users — they'll be able to download artifacts and see the mapping. Note: some evidence documents are operational logs, others are process docs.

[02:58] Rui Chen: When you say controls mapping, is that a crosswalk we already maintain?

[03:05] Maya Patel: We maintain a mapping spreadsheet that cross-references Redwood controls to SOC 2 criteria and ISO 27001 Annex A controls. It's a living doc; I'll share the current version but we expect customers to highlight gaps for their own scope.

[03:28] Aisha Khan: We need to see separation of duties evidence for the ops team and access control proofs — screenshots are fine, but we need logs demonstrating role changes. Do you provide exportable audit logs with user IDs and actions?

[03:45] Maya Patel: Yes, our audit logs capture administrative events — user creation, role assignment, model deployments, key changes. We can export those as JSON lines or CSV. Retention defaults to 90 days on hosted, but for Dedicated/Private customers we can configure retention to 12 months or longer.

[04:10] Tom Becker: So retention depends on deployment mode — if we go Dedicated or Private we get extended retention?

[04:18] Evan Cross: Correct. Hosted standard retention is shorter; Dedicated reserved capacity and Private give more flexibility. For your EU PII requirement we'd recommend either Dedicated in our EU region with customer-managed KMS or Private VPC deployment where you control networking and HSM.

[04:44] Rui Chen: HSM — quick question: can we bring our own key material (BYOK) or do we need to use Redwood-managed keys?

[04:52] Maya Patel: We support three patterns: Redwood-managed keys, Redwood-managed with customer KMS (where customer keys are referenced but Redwood holds wrapped keys), and full EKM where keys stay in the customer's HSM and Redwood calls via an EKM connector. The last option requires Private or dedicated with an EKM connector and some network peering. It's in our integration guide.

[05:20] Aisha Khan: The full EKM option is preferable — that gives us cryptographic control and key separation. What's the attestation for that?

[05:28] Maya Patel: For EKM we provide an architecture diagram and a small set of test calls so you can validate key provenance. We also have audit trails that show key usage events. I'll include the integration note and the HSM vendor caveats — some HSMs require a middleware.

[05:53] Tom Becker: Good. On SSO we have group mapping requirements — we need roles: admin, ops, reader, developer with least privilege. How granular is Redwood RBAC?

[06:05] Maya Patel: RBAC is role-based and fairly granular. We have built-in roles and can add custom roles for Dedicated/Private customers. In hosted we recommend standard roles but you can scope via teams and service accounts. We can demonstrate mapping during the SSO test.

[06:30] Rui Chen: About evidence, will the Trust Center show the exact controls mapped to your process owners? We need to map to our internal control IDs.

[06:40] Maya Patel: The trust center mapping shows our control ID and linked artifacts; it doesn't automatically map to your internal IDs. Typically we provide the crosswalk spreadsheet and customers add their internal control IDs. If you want Redwood to prep an initial mapping to your taxonomy we can, but that would be a professional services add-on.

[07:10] Luis Gray: Quick practical thing — I'll provision the invite for the trust center to the three Cypress emails you shared, read-only. They can download the SOC2 PDF and the control evidence bundle.

[07:25] Aisha Khan: Thanks. We also need the most recent penetration test summary. Is that in Trust Center or separate?

[07:33] Maya Patel: We have a pen test summary (redacted) in the security artifacts; narrows down to high/medium findings and remediation notes. It's in the trust center and linked from the ISO/SOC pack.

[07:50] Tom Becker: Regarding data residency — we operate in EU and US and must ensure data at rest for EU tenants stays in EU. How does Redwood handle multi-region model routing?

[08:02] Evan Cross: We have region-aware routing. For hosted customers you can pin to EU region; Dedicated can deploy in EU region pools; Private you install in your region. We'll document the model fallback behavior; if there's a cross-region failover it's configurable.

[08:24] Rui Chen: If you pin to EU, are any metadata or logs sent to a US control plane?

[08:30] Maya Patel: With our Private option, control plane can be private/within VPC so metadata stays inside. For hosted, we can ensure data plane stays in-region but some telemetry or billing metadata may be in control plane region; we'll flag exactly which fields transit — I'll add that to Evan's note.

[08:55] Aisha Khan: We will need that telemetry list for our privacy impact assessment.

[09:00] Evan Cross: Noted. We'll provide a datum map of what fields are stored where.

[09:15] Tom Becker: On the controls mapping spreadsheet — can you walk through an example?

[09:20] Maya Patel: Sure — open the mapping (screen share simulated in call). For example, our identity management control maps to SOC2 CC6.1 and ISO Annex A.9.2 for access management. There's evidence like SSO configs, MFA enforcement screenshots, and audit logs showing MFA events.

[09:50] Rui Chen: Are logs time-synced to NTP and do you provide timestamp proofs for forensic use?

[09:57] Maya Patel: Yes logs have NTP-synced timestamps, and we can produce time-correlation details in an export.

[10:10] Aisha Khan: We sometimes need continuous exports into our SIEM. Is there a syslog or API integration?

[10:17] Maya Patel: We provide a streaming audit export to customer endpoints (HTTPS webhook, Kafka in Dedicated/Private), and a periodic export for hosted. For SIEM you can use webhook to push events to an aggregator in your VPC.

[10:35] Tom Becker: Nice. For cryptographic controls — you mentioned key rotation. What's the default rotation policy?

[10:42] Maya Patel: Default is annual key rotation for root keys; data encryption keys rotate more frequently depending on tenant settings. With customer-managed keys you control rotation cadence.

[10:58] Evan Cross: I want to call out one tricky piece — model artifacts. If you snapshot a model, is that considered customer data? We treat prompts/outputs as tenant data and can include that in retention policies.

[11:12] Aisha Khan: We'll want to understand whether prompt data ever leaves EU region during inferencing.

[11:18] Maya Patel: With region pinning, inferencing runs in-region. However, cached prefixes or global caches could be a gotcha; our default caching is per-region but there are networked cache options for latency. If you need strict residency, we recommend Private with local-only caching.

[11:40] Tom Becker: For a pilot we'd likely do a staging POC in EU region Dedicated. What are the minimum steps to get the SSO test and trust center access?

[11:50] Evan Cross: Actionable steps: 1) Evan will send SOC2/ISO artifacts; 2) Maya will provision trust center read-only; 3) schedule SAML test; 4) provide KMS integration notes. That should let you validate controls.

[12:05] Rui Chen: If we need an attestation letter for regulatory review, do you provide an AICPA letter or any formal statement?

[12:12] Maya Patel: We can provide the SOC2 Type II report signed by the auditor and an ISO summary. For bespoke attestation language we'd need to coordinate with security/legal, but it's possible with an NDA addendum.

[12:30] Aisha Khan: Good. Also, about incident response — show us the IR playbook snippet. Is that included?

[12:37] Maya Patel: We include IR roles and timelines in our evidence docs; we won't share raw live runbooks, but the playbook summary and post-mortem templates are in trust center.

[12:55] Evan Cross: One more question from my side — competitors. Any particular vendor features that would sway your decision?

[13:02] Tom Becker: Lower latency and BYOK are big ones, but also the clarity of controls mapping for our auditors. If the other vendor had a clear controls crosswalk we might lean that way.

[13:15] Maya Patel: Understood. We'll make the crosswalk as clear as possible and deliver the artifacts promptly.

[13:30] Luis Gray: I'll put the trust center invite in motion now, Evan will send the reports, and Maya will follow up with the SSO scheduling link.

[13:42] Aisha Khan: Anything else on SLA expectations? We need availability SLAs for production (99.95-ish). Is that available for Dedicated?

[13:50] Evan Cross: Yes Dedicated offers SLA tiers with 99.95% uptime and SLO-based credits. We'll include the SLA language with the follow-up email.

[14:05] Rui Chen: Curious about log integrity — do you support WORM or append-only for evidence preservation?

[14:12] Maya Patel: For Private deployments you can enable append-only storage for exported logs; for hosted we provide signed logs and can discuss extended protections as an add-on.

[14:30] Tom Becker: Good. Let's recap next steps.

[14:35] Evan Cross: Recap: Evan share SOC2 + ISO summary by Friday 14th; Maya provision Trust Center read-only by 16th; schedule SSO test for week of 24th; Maya/Evan send KMS/ECM integration notes by 18th; Cypress to review mapping by 21st. Any objections?

[14:55] Aisha Khan: No objections, that timeline looks fine.

[15:00] Rui Chen: We'll review and revert.

[15:05] Evan Cross: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.

[15:10] Luis Gray: Thanks, bye.
[15:12] Tom Becker: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
